page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-96 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 180 GB of system memory. Operating with an allocation of 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, this configuration emphasizes processor density over large working memory footprints. The instance includes no GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage architecture relies entirely on external network volumes, as the instance includes no local storage. The lean memory profile optimizes cost efficiency for applications that would otherwise leave excess memory unutilized, allowing compute-bound systems to maximize core utilization without paying for superfluous RAM capacity.

Given its 96-core parallel capacity and compact memory-to-core ratio, the c4d-highcpu-96 is designed for compute-centric tasks. Suitable workloads include distributed batch processing, automated software compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, video transcoding, and large-scale mathematical simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-96 is a high-density compute instance running on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 180 GB of system memory, the machine delivers a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU. This configuration is tuned for computational density, reducing unneeded memory overhead for CPU-heavy applications. The instance contains no dedicated hardware GPUs and includes no local storage volumes, necessitating remote persistent storage for file system persistence and data management. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine. Given its high core count and compact memory footprint, the c4d-highcpu-96 is well structured for compute-heavy workloads such as distributed batch processing, code compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, video encoding, and multi-threaded analytical computing.
